operationName: Ebola PHEIC Response — 2026 Bundibugyo Outbreak, DRC & Uganda
heroHeadline: Africa CDC & WHO Launch $518M Continental Response Plan as DRC Cases Reach 378 Confirmed
heroSubtitle: By 3 June 2026, the 2026 DRC-Uganda Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak reached 378 total lab-confirmed cases — DRC: 363 (341 Ituri across 17 health zones, 19 Nord-Kivu across 7 health zones, 3 Sud-Kivu) plus Uganda: 15 confirmed (8 Kampala + 1 Wakiso) — with 63 confirmed deaths (62 DRC, 1 Uganda). On June 5, Africa CDC and WHO jointly launched a $518 million Continental Preparedness and Response Plan, the largest African-institution-led outbreak response mobilization in history, aimed at 54 African countries with a focus on 12 high-risk DRC-Uganda neighbors. WHO DG Tedros said on June 3 that the response was 'catching up' but contact tracing coverage at ~45% remains critically below the 90% threshold. Ituri Province expanded to 17 active health zones by June 3 (+2 in 24 hours), with 206 patients currently hospitalized in isolation across DRC. No licensed BDBV vaccine or therapeutic is available; ChAdOx1 BDBV Phase 1 trials are expected within 2–3 months per WHO roadmap. Uganda's DRC border closure entered its ninth day.
footerNote: Data sourced from WHO DG Media Briefing (3 June 2026), WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON602–DON605), Africa CDC–WHO Joint Continental Response Plan (5 June 2026), DRC Ministry of Health (MSANTE), Uganda Ministry of Health, CDC Ebola Situation Summary, ECDC, MSF, NBC News, and ReliefWeb. Case counts are rapidly evolving.
